result:
Here's a draft. I worded it so it doesn't claim more than the script's output shows. "in==out, 0 errors" is the copier's own report, and deleting the old bucket is irreversible. I'd run one independent check before posting, or at least before the deletion date.

**Draft for the team channel**

> **Customer attachments: S3 migration copy finished**
>
> The copy job from `<old-bucket>` to `<new-bucket>` has finished. It reported 48,213 objects copied, in == out, 0 errors.
>
> **Next steps**
> - I'm running an independent comparison of the two buckets (object count, total size, and key listing diff) and will confirm the result here.
> - If the comparison is clean, the plan is to delete `<old-bucket>` next week, on `<date>`.
> - Please reply by `<date - 1 day>` if anything still reads from or writes to the old bucket (app config, presigned URLs, lifecycle rules, scripts, or anything else that references it).
>
> The old bucket will not be deleted until the comparison is confirmed and no one has flagged a dependency.

**Suggested independent check** (run it yourself, since I can't from here):

```
aws s3 ls s3://<old-bucket> --recursive --summarize | tail -2
aws s3 ls s3://<new-bucket> --recursive --summarize | tail -2
```

For a stronger check, diff the sorted key listings, or compare S3 Inventory reports with ETags or checksums. Also confirm that:
- Writes to the old bucket stopped at cutover. Otherwise objects added after the copy won't be in the new one.
- Versioned objects, metadata, ACLs, and encryption settings carried over, if you rely on them.
- The application is actually reading from the new bucket.

Once the check passes, you can drop the "I'm running a comparison" line and change the heading to "migration complete, verified." If you give me the bucket names and deletion date, I can fill in the placeholders.
